proof_summary: Rewrite the coefficient as \(3^n\prod_{t=0}^{n-1}(9t+2)(9t+4)(9t+6)(9t+7)/((3n)!n!)\), and prove denominator divisibility prime by prime. For \(p\ne3\), Legendre’s floor sums are bounded by counting the four corresponding residue classes modulo each \(p^i\) (split according to the modulus modulo \(9\)); for \(p=3\), the factor \(3^n\) together with the factors \(9t+6\) supplies enough powers of \(3\).
